# Florence 1347 – Institutions, law & governance

- **Written, published law code** [`written_law_code`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/written_law_code.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. The statutes of podestà and captain (1322–25) and the Ordinances of Justice (1293) stand beside Roman and canon law. They are Latin, read by lawyers; criers proclaim new decrees. Local: Arte dei Giudici e Notai; Palazzo dei Priori (statute books). Elsewhere: Pisa, the 6th-century Digest manuscript (Pandects); Perugia, Bartolus of Sassoferrato; Bologna, law schools.
- **Rule of law and separation of powers** [`rule_of_law`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/rule_of_law.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept low. Offices rotate and officials are audited, but law is openly unequal: the Ordinances of Justice bar magnate families from office and punish them more harshly on weaker proof. Local: Esecutore degli Ordinamenti di Giustizia; priors and gonfaloniere di giustizia.
- **Independent judges and judicial review** [`independent_judiciary_judicial_review`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/independent_judiciary_judicial_review.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept low. Podestà, captain of the people and executor are hired foreigners on six-month terms, audited on leaving, to keep them above faction. They cannot annul what the councils decree. Local: Palazzo del Podestà; Capitano del Popolo; Esecutore degli Ordinamenti di Giustizia.
- **Habeas corpus and fair trial** [`habeas_corpus_fair_trial`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/habeas_corpus_fair_trial.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Procedure is inquisitorial: secret denunciations dropped in boxes (tamburi), arrest at the judge's will, torture to obtain confession, banishment in absence. Debtors sit in the Stinche. Local: Stinche prison. Elsewhere: England, jury trial and Magna Carta.
- **Representative government (elected assembly)** [`representative_government`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/representative_government.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Since 1343 Florence's widest regime yet: eight priors for two months, most from middle and lesser guilds, beside two councils. Magnates, labourers and the contado are excluded. Local: Palazzo dei Priori; Consiglio del Popolo and Consiglio del Comune; the 21 guilds. Elsewhere: Venice, Great Council (hereditary since 1297); England, Parliament; Aragon and Castile, Cortes.
- **Selection of officials by lot (sortition)** [`sortition`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sortition.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Since 1328 priors and many officers are drawn from bags of approved names. Who gets into the bags is the real contest; the Guelf Party presses to bar 'Ghibellines'. Local: Palazzo dei Priori (the drawings); Parte Guelfa. Elsewhere: Venice, lot and vote combined in electing the doge.
- **Direct democracy (citizen assembly voting on laws)** [`citizen_assembly`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/citizen_assembly.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. A parlamento of all citizens in the piazza is rare and feared: one acclaimed the Duke of Athens lord for life in September 1342. Ordinary laws pass through councils. Local: Piazza dei Priori.
- **Secret ballot** [`secret_ballot`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/secret_ballot.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Councils vote with black beans for yes and white for no, dropped into a bag. Secrecy is imperfect and neighbours watch. Elsewhere: Venice, balloting with balls for the doge and offices.
- **Peaceful transfer of power and loyal opposition** [`peaceful_transfer_of_power`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/peaceful_transfer_of_power.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept low. Offices change hands every two months without violence. Regimes do not: the Duke was driven out by revolt and the magnates by street fighting (1343). Losers are exiled.
- **Written constitution** [`written_constitution`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/written_constitution.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Statutes and the Ordinances of Justice describe the offices and are treated as near-sacred. Any special commission (balìa) can still suspend them.
- **Federalism and subsidiarity** [`federalism_subsidiarity`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/federalism_subsidiarity.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Guelf cities form leagues for war and dissolve them. Arezzo, Pistoia and Volterra threw off Florentine rule in 1343; Pisa holds Lucca. Sharing sovereignty is unthinkable. Elsewhere: Swiss Confederation; Hanseatic towns.
- **Treaties, diplomacy and international law** [`international_law_sovereignty`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/international_law_sovereignty.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Ambassadors go out for single missions; no resident embassies. Treaties are notarised leagues. Foreign courts answer the bank failures with reprisals against any Florentine merchant. The pope arbitrates. Local: chancery of the Signoria; Mercanzia (reprisal cases). Elsewhere: Avignon, Clement VI grants the Canaries to Luis de la Cerda (1344).
- **Secure property rights and land registry** [`property_rights_land_registry`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/property_rights_land_registry.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Title rests on notaries' deeds, registered for the contract tax. The contado is assessed by hearth (estimo). There is no surveyed register; rebels' and bankrupts' property is seized. Local: notaries' registers; gabella dei contratti. Elsewhere: Siena, Tavola delle possessioni (survey of all landed property, 1316–20).
- **Contracts, notaries and merchant courts** [`commercial_law_contract_enforcement`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/commercial_law_contract_enforcement.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Merchant court, guild courts, notaries and account books as proof are among Europe's best. They are now busy with the creditors of the Bardi, Peruzzi and other failed companies. Local: Mercanzia (merchant court, since 1308); Arte dei Giudici e Notai; syndics of the bankrupt companies.
- **Patent law** [`patents`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/patents.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. No patent exists anywhere. Communes lure skilled foreigners with tax exemptions and loans. Guilds forbid monopolies by outsiders and treat methods as the craft's shared secret. Elsewhere: Bologna, privilege for a Lucchese silk-throwing mill (1341); England, royal protection for immigrant Flemish weavers (1331).
- **Copyright for authors** [`copyright`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/copyright.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Anyone may copy any text. Authors live from patrons, benefices or office and complain only of careless scribes.
- **Standard weights and measures** [`standard_weights_measures`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/standard_weights_measures.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Each city has its own braccio, pound and bushel, checked by commune and guilds within its walls. Merchants convert with handbooks such as Pegolotti's. A common system threatens local rights. Local: guild inspectors; Zecca (mint) assayers; grain measures at Orsanmichele; Pegolotti's Pratica della mercatura.
- **Census and registration of births and deaths** [`census_vital_registration`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/census_vital_registration.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The baptistery priest drops a black bean for each boy, a white one for each girl. Bread tickets in April 1347 counted 94,000 mouths. No register of deaths exists. Local: Baptistery of San Giovanni (bean count); Giovanni Villani; grain officials' bread tickets (1347); hearth lists of the contado.
- **Public accounts, audit and budget** [`public_accounts_audit`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/public_accounts_audit.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Officials are audited on leaving office and monks serve as treasurers. Villani could list the commune's revenues item by item. The 1341 war commission's embezzlement is a fresh grievance. Local: Camera del Comune; officials of the Monte; Giovanni Villani's table of revenues and expenses. Elsewhere: Genoa, communal ledgers in double entry (1340).
- **Merit-based civil service (examinations)** [`merit_civil_service`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/merit_civil_service.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept low. The chancellor and the notaries of offices are chosen for skill in Latin and law. Magistrates are drawn by lot from eligible guildsmen; examination for office is unknown. Local: chancery of the Signoria. Elsewhere: China, examinations (reduced under the Yuan).
- **Universal elementary schooling** [`universal_schooling`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/universal_schooling.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept medium. Private masters teach for fees: by Villani's count 8,000–10,000 children at reading, 1,000–1,200 in six abacus schools, about 600 at grammar. Girls rarely go beyond reading; the countryside has little. Local: reading masters; abacus schools (Paolo dell'Abbaco); grammar masters.
- **University (self-governing body of teachers and students)** [`university`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/university.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Florence has no working university; the Studio decreed in 1321 lapsed and is refounded only in 1348–49. Florentines study elsewhere. Teaching is commentary on set texts. Local: Dominican and Franciscan schools of theology; Pisa (Studio chartered 1343); Siena (studium). Elsewhere: Bologna (law, medicine); Padua and Perugia; Paris (theology, arts).
- **Scientific society or academy** [`scientific_academy`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scientific_academy.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Learned men meet in convents and exchange letters; a few Florentines already admire Petrarch. A society that meets to test claims about nature has no model. Local: Augustinians of Santo Spirito; Paolo dell'Abbaco.
- **Organised industrial research laboratory** [`industrial_research_lab`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/industrial_research_lab.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. The wool guild and the cathedral works have skilled men, but capital is scarce after the bank failures and goes to proven work. Local: Arte della Lana; Opera del Duomo. Elsewhere: Venice, the Arsenal.
- **Public library and museum** [`public_library_museum`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/public_library_museum.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Books belong to convents, serving their friars and trusted visitors, and to a few private owners. No library is open to citizens. Ancient statues are curiosities, not collections. Local: libraries of Santa Croce, Santa Maria Novella and Santo Spirito. Elsewhere: Avignon, papal library; Paris, Sorbonne; Cairo and Damascus, endowed madrasa libraries.
- **Freedom of the press** [`free_press`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/free_press.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. No press exists. Words are controlled at the source: statutes punish defaming the regime, the inquisitor watches preaching and books, and criers say what the priors order.
- **Abolition of slavery** [`abolition_of_slavery`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/abolition_of_slavery.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Florence freed its serfs in 1289. Household slaves are still few here; Genoese and Venetians sell Tatar and Circassian captives from Caffa and Tana. Buying unbaptised slaves is held lawful. Elsewhere: Genoa and Venice, slave markets supplied from the Black Sea; Bologna, serfs freed 1256.
- **Women's legal rights and suffrage** [`women_rights_suffrage`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/women_rights_suffrage.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. A woman has dowry and inheritance claims and can make a will, but needs a male guardian (mundualdo) for legal acts. Statutes favour male heirs; no woman holds office.
- **Perpetual endowment (waqf, foundation, trust)** [`charitable_endowment_waqf`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/charitable_endowment_waqf.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Hospitals and confraternities live on endowed farms, houses and bequests. Founding or endowing one earns salvation and honour, and lets usurers make restitution. Local: Santa Maria Nuova; Compagnia di Orsanmichele; Misericordia; Bigallo; hospitals of San Gallo and Santa Maria della Scala (foundlings).
- **Craft guilds and apprenticeship** [`guilds_apprenticeship`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/guilds_apprenticeship.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Twenty-one guilds, seven major and fourteen lesser, control training, quality and entry, and fill the priorate (lesser guilds more since 1343). They block outsiders; wool workers may not organise. Local: Arte della Lana; Arte di Calimala; Arte del Cambio; Arte dei Medici e Speziali; Arte di Por Santa Maria.
- **Permanent public health authority** [`public_health_board`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/public_health_board.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Statutes cover street cleaning, butchers and tanners, and special officials exist for grain. No health office exists anywhere; Venice and Florence appoint temporary plague commissions only in spring 1348. Local: priors and councils (can create a commission by decree); Arte dei Medici e Speziali. Elsewhere: Islamic cities, the muhtasib inspects markets and streets.
- **Fire brigade, civil police and building rules** [`fire_brigade_police_building_codes`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/fire_brigade_police_building_codes.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The foreign magistrates' armed retinues keep order and a curfew bell closes the night. Statutes limit tower heights and overhangs. The fire of 1304 burned some 1,700 houses; no pumps. Local: retinues of podestà, captain and executor; the sixteen neighbourhood companies (gonfaloni).
- **Social insurance and poor relief** [`social_insurance`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/social_insurance.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Guilds and confraternities aid sick members, widows and the poor; in the 1347 famine the commune rationed bread to all. Nothing is a right; labourers outside the guilds get alms. Local: Compagnia di Orsanmichele (alms); Misericordia; guild charity.
- **Trade unions and collective bargaining** [`trade_unions_collective_bargaining`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/trade_unions_collective_bargaining.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Wool workers are subjects of the Arte della Lana and may not assemble. In 1345 the carder Ciuto Brandini was hanged for organising them. Proposing this is sedition.
